content.text:
`entire checkpoint list` is empty because no commit has ever been linked to an agent session yet. The commit named "Add first Entire checkpoint" is just an ordinary git commit; the name doesn't make it a checkpoint. `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows why:

1. **The earlier session started before the repo had any commits.** That session (`803b2e89`) began at 20:45, before your first commit. Entire couldn't set up tracking, and logged `failed to get HEAD: reference not found` and then `skipping checkpoint - will activate after first commit`. So when that session created `hello-entire.md`, Entire wasn't recording it.

2. **Your commit at 20:49 got no checkpoint tag.** Entire's git hooks only make a checkpoint when a tracked session changed the files being committed. They mark that by adding an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line to the end of the commit message. Your commit has no such line, so `entire checkpoint list` has nothing to show.

3. **This session hasn't changed any files.** Tracking does work now (the log shows `initialized shadow session`). But at the end of my first reply it logged `no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint`, because I only ran commands.

**How to get your first real checkpoint:** now that the repo has a commit, any session started from here on is tracked. Have the agent change a file, then commit that change. Entire will add the tag to the commit message and record the session, and it will show up in `entire checkpoint list`.

I can make a small change in this session, such as adding a line to `hello-entire.md`, and commit it so you can watch it work. Want me to?

content.text:
You now have your first real checkpoint.

I added one line to `hello-entire.md` and committed it as `e607c06` on `main`. Entire's git hook added `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4NVZN0MF08RAY3MGHZMCD0Z` to the end of the commit message, and `entire checkpoint list` now shows:

```
checkpoints  1
● 01M4NVZN0MF08RAY3MGHZMCD0Z  "check entire session lsit"
  10-11 21:45 (e607c06) Add checkpoint test line to hello-entire.md
```

The log confirms the rest worked too:
- **Session saved:** this conversation (68 lines) was stored with the checkpoint.
- **Authorship:** the 2 lines in the commit were credited 100% to the agent, since you made no edits of your own.
- **Cleanup:** Entire deleted the temporary branch it uses while a session is in progress (`entire/27eb872-e3b0c4`).

From now on, any commit that includes file changes made during an agent session will get a checkpoint automatically. To see the details of this one:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain 01M4NVZN0MF08RAY3MGHZMCD0Z
```
